main_text.p: refertur, sed ordo potius, aut quicquid il-lud fit, quod inter rem illam & subjectum intercedit. Sic dicit Arist. τὸ ἔχον, quod ad decimam Categ. pertinet, quod haud du-biè denominatio externa est, non esse eum qui vestem habet, nec vestem ipsam, sed τὸ μεταξὺ ἐσότητα, καὶ τῇ ἔχοντος τὴν ἐσότητα. Illud vero quemadmodum non est omni-no nihil, ita quoque non est vera res aut Ens reale, sed medium quippiam inter Ens & nihil. Si enim externa denominatio rem aliquam per se denotaret, sequeretur mu-tari rem omnem & componi, cum ei externa denominatio de novo tribueretur; quod falsum est haud dubiè: nam cum Deus Creator, Conservator, & id genus alia dicitur, denominatio externa est, nec tamen in Deo compositio ex diversis rebus, aut mutatio concedenda est.

VIII. Ex praedictis porro videre est, quomodo externae denominationes distin-guantur à privationibus. Privationes enim remotione habitus connotant aptitudi-nem in subjecto: at denominationes ex-ternae connotant ordinem, quo res externa, unde denominatio sumpta est, ad sub-jectum ordinata est.

page.notes: Greek phrases in the middle of the text (after "sed" and in the "Arist." sentence) are copied from the scan with doubtful accents and letters; the second Greek line is especially uncertain: "ἐσότητα" and "τῇ ἔχοντος" may differ. The first Greek word after "Arist." may also be doubtful. Small marks in the margins and near the bottom (a dash, a tick and dots) are not printed text and were left out. The bottom right catchword "Cap." is partly cut off at the edge and may be longer. The left-hand edge shows a dark mark that is not text.
